# Winifred Tolley

## Overview

- **Age:** 59 years old  <sub>[v5 c26 P26](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0026)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v5 c26 P26](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0026)</sub>

- **Nicknames:** Miss Winifred  <sub>[v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019)</sub>; Mrs. Kerr  <sub>[v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>; Winifred Kerr  <sub>[v5 c25 P12](../source/v05-c25.md#nw-v05-c25-p0012)</sub>

## Appearance

She has a healthy, circular, pink-and-white complexion accompanied by cheerful, brown eyes. Her blonde hair is secured into a rigid, tiny bun tied with a firm elastic band under a sun-hat. She does not reflect the appearance of a conventional old maid.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c27 P35](../source/v04-c27.md#nw-v04-c27-p0035)_

## Personality

Known as having the most venomous tongue and the most compassionate heart in Seven Gulls, Miss Winifred is extremely outspoken, direct, and critical of men. She possesses a sharp tongue, pragmatic views, and a persistent malice and dread toward Methodists. Despite her critical nature, she assists others in the gentlest manner during times of difficulty and is not troubled by nerves.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 c6 P38](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0038), [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c13 P3](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0003)_

## History

Winifred was an only child for eight years before her younger brother was born. Her mother passed away before the boy was three, leaving Winifred to raise him like a mother until he died in his early twenties. Along with other women in the community, she took charge of raising funds and building the Presbyterian church at Glen St. Agnes in six months. She won an award for lemon pies at the Port Marlow Exhibition a decade ago and subsequently retired from making them to protect her reputation. Later, despite being known as a confirmed critic of men, she accepted a proposal from Ambrose Kerr and married him, remaining legally known as Mrs. Ambrose Kerr for thirteen years while maintaining her close ties with friends like Nell Harcourt and Lorna Vane. Later in life, she took Mary Stubbs into her household, maintaining strict discipline over her while developing a deep affection for the girl.

_Sources: [v4 c10 P35](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0035), [v4 c15 P32](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0032), [v4 c34 P26](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0026), [v4 c34 P28](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0028), [v4 c37 P8](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0008), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c9 P0](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0000), [v5 c26 P26](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0026)_
